title: Denormalisation, duplication and writing the same data twice deliberately

videos.script: In a relational schema a duplicated fact is a bug waiting to happen. Here it is a tool. {{tool}} The order page is read hundreds of times a minute. A product's name changes a few times a year. {{ratio}} Copy the name into the order, and every view saves a read. The cost moves to the rare write that changes it. {{move}} But copies are not all the same. The price Ana paid must never change when the price list does. The name the page shows for her must change, everywhere. {{kinds}} In Cassandra the copy is a whole table. One order, written to two tables in one logged batch. You will see what that batch promises, and what it does not. {{batch}} Then the part nobody automates for you. A product is renamed, its copies are updated, and a query counts the copies that did not follow. {{drift}} Writing the same fact twice is fine. Not knowing where you wrote it is the problem.
